Bill number: HB1213
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1132
 By Yarbro

 HOUSE BILL 1213

 By Johnson

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to student assessments.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1403, is amended by deleting

subsection (e) and substituting:

 (e)

 (1) A parent of a participating student:

 (A) Shall ensure that the participating student is annually

 administered all Tennessee comprehensive assessment program (TCAP)

 tests, or successor tests authorized by the state board of education, that

 are administered to a public school student in the same grade or same

 course subject as the participating student;

 (B) In grade eleven (11) shall ensure that the student is

 administered the examination that is administered to public school

 students in grade (11) pursuant to § 49-6-6001(b)(1); and

 (C) In any of the grades kindergarten through three (K-3) shall

 ensure that the participating student is annually administered each of the

 three (3) Tennessee universal reading screeners, or universal reading

 screeners approved by the state board of education, as described in § 49-

 1-905(c) during each of the three (3) administration windows established

 by the department of education pursuant to § 49-1-905(c)(1).

 (2) A participating student's results on the tests administered pursuant to

 this subsection (e) must be reported to the parent of the student.

 (3) Students with disabilities who would have participated in the alternate

 assessments, as determined on the student's IEP, are exempt from the

 requirements in this subsection (e).

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2606(a)(1), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (1) As a condition of participating in the program:

 (A) Participating students must be annually administered the Tennessee

 comprehensive assessment program (TCAP) tests, or successor tests authorized

 by the state board of education, that are administered to a public school student

 in the same grade or same course subject as the participating student;

 (B) Participating students in grade eleven (11) must be administered the

 examination that is administered to public schools students in grade eleven (11)

 pursuant to § 49-6-6001(b)(1); and

 (C) Participating students in kindergarten through grade three (K-3) must

 annually be administered each of the three (3) Tennessee universal reading

 screeners, or universal reading screeners approved by the state board of

 education, as described in § 49-1-905(c) during each of the three (3)

 administration windows established by the department of education pursuant to §

 49-1-905(c)(1).

 SECTION 3. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would change testing rules for students in two Tennessee school choice programs. It rewrites Section 49-10-1403(e) and Section 49-6-2606(a)(1) of the state code, which cover participating students. The bill text does not name the programs, so they are called "the programs" here.

Under the first change, a parent of a participating student would have to make sure the student takes, each year, all Tennessee comprehensive assessment program (TCAP) tests, or successor tests authorized by the state board of education. These are the tests given to public school students in the same grade or course subject. A parent of a student in grade eleven would also have to make sure the student takes the exam given to public school eleventh graders under § 49-6-6001(b)(1). A parent of a student in kindergarten through grade three would have to make sure the student takes each of the three Tennessee universal reading screeners, or screeners approved by the state board of education. The student would take each one during each of the three administration windows set by the department of education. Test results would have to be reported to the parent. Students with disabilities who would have taken alternate assessments, as set by their IEP, would be exempt from these requirements.

Under the second change, the same testing rules would become conditions of participating in the program: annual TCAP or successor tests, the grade eleven exam, and the three reading screeners in kindergarten through grade three. The text of this second change does not include the disability exemption or the results-reporting rule.

The act would take effect July 1, 2025.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: Under the first change, a parent of a participating student would have to make sure the student takes, each year, all Tennessee comprehensive assessment program (TCAP) tests, or successor tests authorized by the state board of education. These are the tests given to public school students in the same grade or course subject.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the parent's duty, annual testing, authorized successors, and grade-or-course matching. The summary identifies the amended subsection and separately states its disability exemption.

assessments.summary_quote: A parent of a student in grade eleven would also have to make sure the student takes the exam given to public school eleventh graders under § 49-6-6001(b)(1).
assessments.rationale: States the parent's duty, grade, and required examination. The disability exemption is stated later in the same paragraph.

assessments.summary_quote: A parent of a student in kindergarten through grade three would have to make sure the student takes each of the three Tennessee universal reading screeners, or screeners approved by the state board of education. The student would take each one during each of the three administration windows set by the department of education.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the parent obligation, grades, screeners, approved alternatives, and administration windows, with the exemption stated separately. It does not specify that reading screening must occur annually; the earlier annual language applies expressly to TCAP tests.

assessments.summary_quote: Test results would have to be reported to the parent.
assessments.rationale: In context, this states the reporting requirement for tests under the first replacement subsection.

assessments.summary_quote: Students with disabilities who would have taken alternate assessments, as set by their IEP, would be exempt from these requirements.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the disability exemption, its alternate-assessment eligibility condition, the IEP determination, and its application to the subsection's requirements.

assessments.summary_quote: Under the second change, the same testing rules would become conditions of participating in the program: annual TCAP or successor tests, the grade eleven exam, and the three reading screeners in kindergarten through grade three.
assessments.rationale: States annual TCAP or successor testing as a participation condition. 'The same testing rules' incorporates the preceding state-board authorization and grade-or-course matching requirements, and the amendment target is identified earlier.
